title: Sarf Foundations
subtitle: Master the patterns and forms of Arabic morphology
description: A three-level journey through classical Sarf (Arabic morphology) — from root types and basic conjugation, through augmented verb forms and weak roots, to the deepest patterns of derivation and irregularity.

stages.title: I'lāl in Derived Nouns
stages.description: How weak-letter changes carry into Ism al-Fā'il, Maf'ūl, and more

questions.text: What happens to the Ism al-Fā'il of an Ajwaf (hollow) root like قَالَ?
options: The middle weak letter converts to a hamzah
It stays completely unchanged as قَاوِل
questions.answer: The middle weak letter converts to a hamzah

questions.text: What is the Ism al-Maf'ūl of a Nāqiṣ (weak-final) root like رَمَى, in its basic form?
options: مَرْمِيّ (marmiyy), with the weak letter converting and doubling
questions.answer: مَرْمِيّ (marmiyy), with the weak letter converting and doubling

questions.text: What is the Ism al-Fā'il of دَعَا (a Nāqiṣ root)?
options: دَاعٍ (dā'in) — following the Ism Manqūṣ pattern
questions.answer: دَاعٍ (dā'in) — following the Ism Manqūṣ pattern

questions.text: Why does I'lāl in derived nouns often connect back to the Manqūṣ/Maqṣūr noun categories?
options: Because the weak letters in derived nouns often produce exactly those noun-ending patterns
Because all derived nouns are automatically Jāmid
Because derived nouns are always Mabnī
questions.answer: Because the weak letters in derived nouns often produce exactly those noun-ending patterns

questions.text: What is the Maṣdar of قَالَ (a hollow/Ajwaf root)?
options: قَوْل (qawl) — the middle weak letter surfaces as a consonant وْ here
questions.answer: قَوْل (qawl) — the middle weak letter surfaces as a consonant وْ here

stages.title: One Root, Many Meanings
stages.description: How the same root shifts meaning across different Mazīd forms

questions.text: From the root س-ل-م, what does أَسْلَمَ (Form IV) mean?
options: "To submit/surrender [to Allah]" — a shift toward a specific religious sense
questions.answer: "To submit/surrender [to Allah]" — a shift toward a specific religious sense

questions.text: From the same root س-ل-م, what does سَلَّمَ (Form II) commonly mean?
From the root ع-ل-م, what does عَلَّمَ (Form II) mean, compared to عَلِمَ (bare root, "to know")?
From the root ع-ل-م, what does تَعَلَّمَ (Form V) mean?
options: "To learn" (reflexive — to cause oneself to know)
questions.answer: "To learn" (reflexive — to cause oneself to know)

questions.text: Why is tracing one root across all its Mazīd forms a valuable advanced Sarf exercise?
options: It reveals the underlying logic connecting a whole family of related words and meanings
It only helps with memorizing the Mīzān
It only matters for weak roots
It replaces the need to learn Nahw
questions.answer: It reveals the underlying logic connecting a whole family of related words and meanings

stages.title: Ism al-Marrah wal-Hay'ah
stages.description: Nouns of single occurrence and of manner

questions.text: What does Ism al-Marrah express?
options: A single occurrence of an action ("one time")
The tool used for an action
questions.answer: A single occurrence of an action ("one time")

questions.text: What is the pattern of Ism al-Marrah from a bare triliteral root?
ضَرْبَة (ḍarbah — "a single hit/strike") is the Ism al-Marrah of which root?
What does Ism al-Hay'ah express?
options: The manner or style in which an action was performed
questions.answer: The manner or style in which an action was performed

questions.text: What is the pattern of Ism al-Hay'ah from a bare triliteral root?
جِلْسَة (jilsah — "a manner/way of sitting") is the Ism al-Hay'ah of which root?

stages.title: Advanced Synthesis
stages.description: Deriving every major form from a single given root

questions.text: Given the root ك-ر-م ("to be noble/generous"), which Bāb does كَرُمَ belong to?
What is the Ism al-Fā'il-family word (Ṣifah Mushabbahah) for "generous" from ك-ر-م?
What is the Ism at-Tafḍīl from ك-ر-م ("more/most generous")?
What is the Form IV verb from ك-ر-م, meaning "to honor [someone]"?
What is the Ism al-Maf'ūl of أَكْرَمَ ("one who is honored")?
Putting it all together — which Sarf skill lets you predict كَرِيم, أَكْرَم, أَكْرَمَ, and مُكْرَم all from the single root ك-ر-م؟
options: Recognizing patterns (awzān) and applying them systematically to any root
Memorizing every word individually with no system
Only Nahw can explain this, not Sarf
questions.answer: Recognizing patterns (awzān) and applying them systematically to any root
